prompt: A company's newly formed Digital Transformation Program Management Office (PMO) needs a scorecard to report progress to the executive team monthly. Design 4-6 KPIs.
context: The transformation program spans 12 workstreams of varying size and maturity. Previous ad hoc reporting (before the PMO existed) consisted only of each workstream lead self-reporting a "red/yellow/green" status, which the CFO has noted was "almost always green until it suddenly wasn't" — several workstreams reported green status for months before revealing major delays. The program has a fixed, board-approved budget and a set of milestone dates; 3 of the 12 workstreams are on the critical path for a public commitment made to investors about a launch date.

binaryCriteria.description: Includes objective, harder-to-game measures (e.g., schedule variance, budget burn-rate vs. plan) rather than relying solely on subjective self-reported RAG status.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the proposed scorecard consists only of a (possibly relabeled) self-reported status color with no objective schedule/budget measure.

binaryCriteria.description: Explicitly gives the 3 critical-path workstreams (tied to the investor launch-date commitment) a distinct, more scrutinized tracking treatment compared to the other 9 workstreams.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if all 12 workstreams are treated identically with no distinction for the critical-path ones.

binaryCriteria.description: Explicitly connects at least one proposed KPI to solving the specific "green until it suddenly wasn't" credibility problem the CFO raised.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the scorecard design does not address why the previous RAG-only approach failed to give early warning.

goldNotes: A strong scorecard directly addresses the CFO's "green until it suddenly wasn't" complaint by including objective, leading indicators rather than relying solely on subjective self-reported RAG status — e.g., milestone-schedule variance (actual vs. planned dates, a factual/objective measure) and budget burn-rate versus plan (also objective), which are harder to game than a subjective color rating. It should explicitly call out the 3 critical-path workstreams as needing a distinct, more frequent or more scrutinized tracking cut (since they carry investor-commitment risk), rather than treating all 12 workstreams identically in the reporting cadence. A weak scorecard just re-proposes the same self-reported RAG status (possibly relabeled) without adding any objective, harder-to-game measure, which would fail to address the specific credibility problem the CFO raised.
